components.title: postgresql-ubi
components.description: A PostgreSQL 18 container component built from PGDG packages on Red Hat UBI 9.
components.purpose: Supply a reproducible restricted-runtime database image; system controls remain shared with the deployment, host, and organization.

control-implementations.description: Selected component-relevant NIST controls mapped to reviewed DISA and upstream requirements. This is not a system implementation or assessment.

implemented-requirements.description: The component supports PostgreSQL role, database, schema, and object authorization; the deployment defines identities and grants.

props.name: classification
props.value: deployment-supported

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST AC-3; SRG-APP-000033-DB-000084

props.name: rationale
props.value: PostgreSQL supplies authorization mechanisms but no image can choose application privileges.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Excessive grants or superuser use can bypass intended separation.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md

props.name: owner
props.value: deployment-owner

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine role/grant policy; test denied and permitted operations; interview database owner

props.name: default-state
props.value: Bootstrap creates only the requested initial superuser and database.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Roles, memberships, ownership, default privileges, and row security are deployment data.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Approved role model and application identities.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Grant changes normally take effect without container restart.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Least privilege can expose undeclared application dependencies.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Superuser, ownership, or broad PUBLIC grants defeat access boundaries.

props.name: limitations
props.value: The image does not provision an organization-specific authorization model.

implemented-requirements.description: PostgreSQL emits operational logs to container stdout; event selection and centralized audit retention are deployment functions.

props.name: classification
props.value: deployment-supported

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST AU-2; SRG-APP-000091-DB-000066

props.name: rationale
props.value: The database can emit selected events while the runtime and SIEM collect and retain them.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Insufficient event selection or collector loss can leave investigation gaps.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/RUNTIME-SECURITY.md

props.name: owner
props.value: deployment-owner

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine logging configuration; test selected events and interruption; interview SIEM owner

props.name: default-state
props.value: Server logs go to stderr with the PostgreSQL default event set.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Event classes, detail, prefix, duration, and collector behavior are configurable.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Runtime log driver, capacity, access control, clock, and SIEM policy.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Most logging settings reload; collector changes may require restart.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Verbose SQL logging can expose data and increase I/O and storage demand.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Disabled, dropped, uncorrelated, or mutable logs remove accountability evidence.

props.name: limitations
props.value: The image has no SIEM, retention, immutable storage, or organization event policy.

implemented-requirements.description: The repository fixes a minimal image baseline with locked input artifacts and restricted-runtime defaults.

props.name: classification
props.value: image-owned

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST CM-2; RHEL 9 STIG V2R9 baseline concepts; SRG-APP-000516-CTR-001325

props.name: rationale
props.value: The repository controls packages, files, entrypoint, metadata, and tested defaults.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Host, runtime, mounted configuration, and initialized data alter the effective system baseline.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/ARTIFACT-ACQUISITION.md

props.name: owner
props.value: maintainer

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine locks and image manifest; test native builds and restricted runtime; interview maintainer

props.name: default-state
props.value: Digest-pinned UBI stages, exact RPM closure, no package manager metadata, nonroot runtime.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Deployment may add configuration and mounts but must not mutate the image.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Verified artifact bundle and protected CI inputs.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: A baseline change requires rebuild and full requalification.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Minimal tooling makes interactive repair and diagnostics intentionally limited.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Mutable tags, unlocked inputs, or writable root filesystems destroy baseline identity.

props.name: limitations
props.value: This is a component baseline, not a RHEL host baseline or DISA-approved configuration.

implemented-requirements.description: The image documents consistent backup interfaces; backup execution, encryption, custody, and restore objectives are inherited.

props.name: classification
props.value: inherited

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST CP-9; Database SRG V4R5 backup requirements

props.name: rationale
props.value: Only the deployment knows durability, recovery objectives, keys, media, and restore location.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Missing, stolen, inconsistent, or untested backups can cause disclosure or irreversible loss.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/STORAGE.md

props.name: owner
props.value: organization-owner

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine backup records; test isolated restore and integrity; interview storage and recovery owners

props.name: default-state
props.value: No automatic backup service is included.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Logical, physical, WAL, snapshot, encryption, and retention design is external.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Durable volume, backup system, protected keys, capacity, RPO and RTO.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Backup configuration depends on method; restore normally replaces a stopped instance.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Backup and restore consume I/O, storage, time, and may require quiescence.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Untested or inaccessible recovery material eliminates recoverability.

props.name: limitations
props.value: Image tests demonstrate mechanics only, not organization recovery objectives.

implemented-requirements.description: The image requires a bootstrap secret and defaults PostgreSQL passwords and host rules to SCRAM-SHA-256; lifecycle policy is external.

props.name: classification
props.value: deployment-supported

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST IA-5; SRG-APP-000171-DB-000074; PostgreSQL 18 password authentication

props.name: rationale
props.value: The image enforces safe bootstrap transport and hashing; the organization creates and rotates secrets.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Weak, reused, exposed, or unrotated passwords remain possible.

props.name: evidence
props.value: tests/runtime-security.sh

props.name: owner
props.value: deployment-owner

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine secret and HBA configuration; test missing secret and SCRAM login; interview secret owner

props.name: default-state
props.value: Secret file required on first initialization; SCRAM-SHA-256 selected; trust rejected.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: External HBA and server configuration can change authentication and iteration count.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Runtime secret service with correct ownership, mode, rotation, and audit.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: HBA reload is sufficient; role password rotation is online; bootstrap secret is initialization-only.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Rotation and stronger hashing can affect clients and authentication latency.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Trust, cleartext network password use, leaked secret files, or stale roles enable compromise.

props.name: limitations
props.value: No password breach-list service, MFA, or enterprise identity provider is included.

implemented-requirements.description: The repository provides withdrawal and evidence-preservation procedures; incident command and notification are organization-owned.

props.name: classification
props.value: inherited

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST IR-4; NIST SP 800-53A examine/test/interview method

props.name: rationale
props.value: A public component maintainer cannot operate a consumer incident response program.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Delayed coordination can expand compromise and evidence loss.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md

props.name: owner
props.value: organization-owner

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine plan and rehearsal; test contact and quarantine path; interview incident owner

props.name: default-state
props.value: Private reporting and maintainer withdrawal procedures are documented.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Consumer severity, legal notification, evidence, and containment plans are external.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Named responders, monitored contacts, registry authority, backups, and legal policy.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Containment may stop service; recovery uses a new qualified digest and rotated credentials.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Containment and evidence preservation can interrupt database availability.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Moving tags, deleting evidence, or reusing credentials compromises recovery confidence.

props.name: limitations
props.value: The maintainer does not know consumer contacts, data, law, or infrastructure.

implemented-requirements.description: The image supports PostgreSQL TLS but leaves certificate issuance, trust, client verification, and ingress enforcement to deployment.

props.name: classification
props.value: deployment-supported

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST SC-8; SRG-APP-000441-DB-000378

props.name: rationale
props.value: TLS capability is inside PostgreSQL; certificates and network enforcement are deployment-specific.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Clients can be spoofed or traffic exposed if TLS or verification is optional.

props.name: evidence
props.value: tests/tls.sh

props.name: owner
props.value: deployment-owner

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine certificate/HBA/client policy; test TLS and plaintext rejection; interview PKI owner

props.name: default-state
props.value: TLS is not enabled without deployment-provided key, certificate, HBA, and configuration.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: TLS versions, ciphers, CA, client certificates, HBA and client sslmode are configurable.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Protected server key, valid certificate chain, trusted time, DNS, and client trust.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Initial enablement requires restart; certificate/configuration reload behavior must be rehearsed.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Strict verification can reject misnamed, expired, or untrusted certificates.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Plain host records, sslmode disable/prefer, or key compromise remove transport assurance.

props.name: limitations
props.value: TLS support is not a FIPS validation or proof of client policy.

implemented-requirements.description: Cryptographic mechanisms are inventoried, but no FIPS validation claim is made for this image or PostgreSQL configuration.

props.name: classification
props.value: research-required

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST SC-13; SRG-APP-000179-DB-000114; RHEL 9 STIG V2R9

props.name: rationale
props.value: A claim requires exact library linkage, provider mode, architecture, runtime context, and applicable CMVP certificate.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Operators may mistake UBI origin, TLS, or host FIPS mode for validated image cryptography.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/CRYPTOGRAPHIC-BOUNDARY.md

props.name: owner
props.value: maintainer

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine binaries, providers and CMVP records; test each architecture/mode; interview cryptographic authority

props.name: default-state
props.value: No FIPS or validated-cryptography claim.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Host mode, OpenSSL providers, PostgreSQL TLS, SCRAM, checksums, and signing are separate boundaries.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Exact release digest and architecture plus verified module, provider, host, and CMVP evidence.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Mode/provider/TLS changes can require host and database restart and requalification.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Approved algorithms and provider modes may reduce compatibility or performance.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Unapproved providers, algorithms, key handling, or boundary changes invalidate a claim.

props.name: limitations
props.value: No applicable CMVP certificate or tested end-to-end mode is established.

implemented-requirements.description: The project monitors suppliers, locks exact inputs, scans both architectures, and defines time-bound remediation and withdrawal decisions.

props.name: classification
props.value: image-owned

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST SI-2; SRG-APP-000456-DB-000390

props.name: rationale
props.value: Maintainers own component input monitoring, rebuild, qualification, and release withdrawal.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Unknown, unfixed, disputed, or deployment-specific exposure can remain.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/VULNERABILITY-MANAGEMENT.md

props.name: owner
props.value: maintainer

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine advisories, scans and exceptions; test rebuild/withdrawal; interview triage owner

props.name: default-state
props.value: Fixed High/Critical findings block; scheduled monitoring and two scanners are configured.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Exceptions require exact digest/architecture, approval, expiry and rescan trigger.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Current PGDG, PostgreSQL, Red Hat and scanner data plus monitored private reports.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Correction requires a new immutable image digest and deployment rollout.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Urgent withdrawal or update can interrupt planned change windows.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Stale databases, blanket ignores, moving tags, or bypassed qualification defeat remediation.

props.name: limitations
props.value: Scanners do not prove reachability, absence of design flaws, or deployment patching.

implemented-requirements.description: The build verifies publisher signatures, checksums, source-to-binary mappings, exact package closures, SBOMs, provenance, and release signatures.

props.name: classification
props.value: image-owned

props.name: source-requirement
props.value: NIST SR-4; Container Platform SRG supply-chain requirements

props.name: rationale
props.value: Repository workflows own acquisition verification and evidence for produced images.

props.name: residual-risk
props.value: Supplier, signing-key, CI runner, registry, or evidence systems can still be compromised.

props.name: evidence
props.value: docs/RELEASE.md

props.name: owner
props.value: maintainer

props.name: review-status
props.value: pending-independent-review

props.name: assessment-method
props.value: examine locks/provenance/signatures; test tampered input and independent verification; interview release owner

props.name: default-state
props.value: Exact hashes, fingerprints, actions, scanners, native architectures, and immutable release identity.

props.name: configurable-state
props.value: Any supplier, key, package, action, tool, or base closure change requires reviewed lock update.

props.name: prerequisites
props.value: Protected branch, trusted GitHub identities, supplier keys, registry, OIDC and evidence retention.

props.name: restart-behavior
props.value: Input changes produce a new digest; consumers must explicitly roll out that digest.

props.name: operational-impact
props.value: Fail-closed verification can delay builds and releases.

props.name: loss-of-protection
props.value: Unverified mirrors, mutable refs, compromised keys/runners, or missing evidence break traceability.

props.name: limitations
props.value: Provenance establishes recorded build inputs, not supplier or CI infallibility.
